title: Helper Lemmas: Nonnegativity and Nonzero Denominators
content: Redeclares key infrastructure as private lemmas since the originals in the main Feuerbach file are private. Establishes that dist2 and ninePointRadius are nonneg, the circumcenter denominator $d = 2[(A_x - C_x)(B_y - C_y) - (B_x - C_x)(A_y - C_y)]$ is nonzero (from non-degeneracy), and all squared side lengths $|BC|^2, |CA|^2, |AB|^2$ are nonzero. These are the denominators that appear when unfolding coordinate definitions, and clearing them is essential for the field_simp + ring strategy.
mathContext: The circumcenter denominator $d = 2\det\begin{pmatrix} A-C \\ B-C \end{pmatrix}$ is twice the signed area of the triangle. Non-degeneracy ($d \neq 0$) is equivalent to the three vertices not being collinear.

title: Altitude Feet on the Nine-Point Circle
content: Three theorems proving that each altitude foot lies on the nine-point circle: $d(N, H_a) = d(N, H_b) = d(N, H_c) = R/2$. Each proof follows the same elegant strategy: (1) reduce to squared distance equality via eq_of_sq_eq_nonneg, (2) eliminate sqrt via Real.sq_sqrt, (3) unfold foot definitions (orthogonal projection onto opposite side) and nine-point center (midpoint of circumcenter and orthocenter), (4) establish nonzero denominators, (5) clear all fractions with field_simp and verify the resulting polynomial identity with ring. These three theorems eliminate 3 of the 8 original axioms from the main Feuerbach formalization.
mathContext: The altitude foot $H_a$ is the orthogonal projection of vertex $A$ onto side $BC$. In coordinates, $H_a = B + \frac{(A-B) \cdot (C-B)}{|C-B|^2}(C-B)$. The nine-point center is $N = (O + H)/2$ where $O$ is the circumcenter and $H$ is the orthocenter.

title: Equilateral Triangle: R = 2r
content: Constructs the equilateral triangle with vertices $(0,0)$, $(s,0)$, $(s/2, s\sqrt{3}/2)$ and proves all side lengths equal $s$, semiperimeter $= 3s/2$, area $= s^2\sqrt{3}/4$, inradius $= s\sqrt{3}/6$, circumcenter $= (s/2, s\sqrt{3}/6)$. The key insight is working with squared quantities: $R^2 = s^2/4 + s^2 \cdot 3/36 = s^2/3$ and $(2r)^2 = (s\sqrt{3}/3)^2 = s^2/3$, avoiding direct sqrt arithmetic. This eliminates the 4th axiom from the original formalization.
mathContext: For equilateral triangles, $R = 2r$ means the nine-point circle and incircle coincide (both have center at the centroid with radius $R/2 = r$). This is the degenerate case of Feuerbach's theorem where internal tangency becomes coincidence: $d(N,I) = |R/2 - r| = 0$.

title: 3-4-5 Triangle: Numerical Excircle Verification
content: Verifies all three excircle tangency relations for the 3-4-5 right triangle. Computes excenters $I_a = (6,6)$, $I_b = (-3,3)$, $I_c = (2,-2)$ and exradii $r_a = 6$, $r_b = 3$, $r_c = 2$ via the formulas $r_k = \text{Area}/(s - k)$. Each verification reduces to checking that $\sqrt{\text{known value}} = R/2 + r_k$ using norm_num. This served as a validation step before attempting the general proofs.
mathContext: For the 3-4-5 triangle: $R = 5/2$ (hypotenuse/2), $s = 6$, Area $= 6$, $r = 1$. The excircle tangencies: $d(N, I_a) = 29/4 = 5/4 + 6$, $d(N, I_b) = 17/4 = 5/4 + 3$, $d(N, I_c) = 13/4 = 5/4 + 2$.

title: Algebraic Backbone: Positivity, Sigma Identity, Extended Law of Sines
content: Proves the foundational results needed for the general Feuerbach proof: (1) area, semiperimeter, and inradius are all positive for nondegenerate triangles; (2) the sigma identity $\sigma = abcs - 4s(s-a)(s-b)(s-c)$ by pure ring computation; (3) the extended law of sines in squared form $a^2 b^2 c^2 = 16R^2 \cdot \text{Area}^2$ by unfolding all definitions and using field_simp + ring; (4) Euler's formula $OI^2 = R^2 - 2Rr$ verified for the 3-4-5 triangle.
mathContext: The sigma expression $\sigma = (s-a)(s-b)c^2 + (s-a)(s-c)b^2 + (s-b)(s-c)a^2$ arises from the bilinear expansion of $|N-I|^2$. The extended law of sines $abc = 4R \cdot \text{Area}$ connects side lengths to the circumradius and is the key substitution in the algebraic chain.

title: Heron's Formula and Circumcenter Dot Products
content: Proves Heron's formula in three equivalent forms: (1) squared polynomial $16 \cdot \text{Area}^2 = 2a^2b^2 + 2b^2c^2 + 2c^2a^2 - a^4 - b^4 - c^4$, (2) product $(a+b+c)(b+c-a)(a+c-b)(a+b-c) = 16\text{Area}^2$, (3) classical $\text{Area}^2 = s(s-a)(s-b)(s-c)$. Also proves circumcenter dot product identities $\langle A-O, B-O \rangle = R^2 - c^2/2$ using the polarization identity $\langle u,v\rangle = (|u|^2 + |v|^2 - |u-v|^2)/2$ and the equidistance property $|OA| = |OB| = |OC| = R$.
mathContext: The polarization identity relates inner products to distances: $\langle P-R, Q-R \rangle = \frac{|RP|^2 + |RQ|^2 - |PQ|^2}{2}$. Applied to the circumcenter where $|OA| = |OB| = R$, this yields $\langle A-O, B-O \rangle = R^2 - |AB|^2/2 = R^2 - c^2/2$.

title: Feuerbach Algebraic Core: The Key Substitution
content: The heart of Feuerbach's theorem: proves $R^2 s^2 - \sigma = (Rs - 2\text{Area})^2$ by substituting $abc = 4R \cdot \text{Area}$ into the sigma expression. This is a purely algebraic manipulation: $R^2s^2 - (abcs - 4\text{Area}^2) = R^2s^2 - 4R \cdot \text{Area} \cdot s + 4\text{Area}^2 = (Rs - 2\text{Area})^2$. Combined with the bilinear expansion showing $4s^2 |NI|^2 = R^2 s^2 - \sigma$, this gives $|NI|^2 = (Rs - 2\text{Area})^2/(4s^2) = (R/2 - r)^2$.
mathContext: The substitution $abcs \to 4R \cdot \text{Area} \cdot s$ via the extended law of sines is the key algebraic trick. It converts a complex expression involving products of three side lengths into a perfect square in $R$ and Area, which are the "right" variables for expressing the Feuerbach distance.

title: Triangle Inequalities from Heron's Formula
content: Proves $s - a > 0$, $s - b > 0$, $s - c > 0$ (the classical triangle inequalities in semiperimeter form) using a beautiful indirect argument: Heron's formula gives $\text{Area}^2 = s(s-a)(s-b)(s-c)$ and area is positive, so the product is positive. Since $s > 0$, if any factor $s - k \leq 0$, then the other two factors are nonneg (because $k \geq a+b$ would imply $s-a, s-b \geq 0$), making the product $\leq 0$ — contradiction.
mathContext: The triangle inequality $a < b + c$ is equivalent to $s - a > 0$ where $s = (a+b+c)/2$. The proof from Heron avoids coordinate computation entirely — it's a purely algebraic consequence of area positivity.

title: NI Vector Formula and Bilinear Expansion
content: The geometric-algebraic bridge. First proves the NI vector formula: $2s(N - I) = (s-a)(A-O) + (s-b)(B-O) + (s-c)(C-O)$, which expresses the nine-point-center-to-incenter vector in terms of vertex-to-circumcenter vectors weighted by semiperimeter defects. Then expands the squared norm using bilinear form to get $4s^2|NI|^2 = \sum (s-k)^2 R^2 + 2\sum_{i<j} (s-k_i)(s-k_j) \langle V_i-O, V_j-O \rangle$. Substituting the circumcenter dot products and applying the algebraic chain yields the key identity $4s^2|NI|^2 = (Rs - 2\text{Area})^2$.
mathContext: The NI vector formula follows from $N = (O+H)/2$ (nine-point center is midpoint of circumcenter and orthocenter) and $I = (aA + bB + cC)/(a+b+c)$ (incenter via barycentric coordinates). The identity $H = A + B + C - 2O$ for the orthocenter in coordinates makes this a polynomial identity provable by ring.

title: Feuerbach's Theorem: Incircle Distance (General Proof)
content: The main result for the incircle: $d(N, I) = |R/2 - r|$. From feuerbach_NI_sq which establishes $|NI|^2 = (R/2 - r)^2$ (combining all the algebraic and geometric machinery), takes the square root using Real.sqrt_sq_eq_abs. This single theorem eliminates the incircle distance axiom from the parent formalization and proves internal tangency of the nine-point circle and incircle for all triangles.
mathContext: $d(N, I) = |R/2 - r|$ means internal tangency: the nine-point circle (center $N$, radius $R/2$) is internally tangent to the incircle (center $I$, radius $r$). The absolute value handles both cases: $R/2 > r$ (generic) and $R/2 = r$ (equilateral, where the circles coincide).

title: Excircle Distance Proofs (All Three)
content: Proves $d(N, I_k) = R/2 + r_k$ for all three excircles ($k = a, b, c$) using the same algebraic framework as the incircle proof but with modified vector formulas. For excircle $I_a$, the vector formula is $2(s-a)(N - I_a) = s(A-O) - (s-c)(B-O) - (s-b)(C-O)$ (note the sign changes reflecting that the excircle is opposite vertex $A$). Each proof chain: vector formula → bilinear expansion → sigma-variant identity → algebraic core → squared distance → take sqrt. The three excircle proofs together with the incircle proof eliminate ALL 4 remaining Feuerbach distance axioms.
mathContext: External tangency $d(N, I_k) = R/2 + r_k$ means the nine-point circle and each excircle touch from the outside. The excircle opposite $A$ has center $I_a = (-aA + bB + cC)/(-a+b+c)$ and radius $r_a = \text{Area}/(s-a)$. The plus sign (vs absolute value for incircle) reflects external tangency.
